quarterly_data.signal: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: Q2 2026 revenue was TWD 1,097 million, up 0.2% sequentially and up 17.1% year over year; operating expenses TWD 431 million; operating income TWD 666 million (up 0.6% QoQ, up 22% YoY); operating margin 60.7% (up 0.2 percentage points QoQ, up 2.4 percentage points YoY); net income TWD 580 million (down 2.8% QoQ, up 44.9% YoY); EPS TWD 7.77.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue TWD 1,097 million (+0.2% QoQ, +17.1% YoY); operating income TWD 666 million; operating margin 60.7%; net income TWD 580 million (+44.9% YoY); EPS TWD 7.77

quarterly_data.signal: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: Q2 2026 licensing was 39.2% of revenue, up 12.8% QoQ and 35.1% YoY; royalty was 60.8% of revenue, down 6.4% QoQ but up 7.8% YoY. First half 2026: licensing 37% of revenue, up 45.2% YoY; royalty 63% of revenue, up 7% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 licensing 39.2% of revenue (+12.8% QoQ, +35.1% YoY); Q2 royalty 60.8% (-6.4% QoQ, +7.8% YoY); 1H licensing +45.2% YoY, 1H royalty +7% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia, Q2 2026 revenue by technology: NeoFuse (OTP) 56.6% of total revenue (licensing up 24.8% QoQ and 55.6% YoY; royalty down 13.3% QoQ, up 4.4% YoY); NeoBit 21.9%; PUF-based security IP 10.9% (licensing up 133.5% YoY; PUF royalty up 213.9% QoQ and over 1,600% YoY); MTP 10.6% (royalty up 19.2% YoY). First half 2026: PUF-based security IP 11.6% of revenue, licensing up 264.6% YoY and royalty up over 1,300% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: NeoFuse 56.6%; NeoBit 21.9%; PUF-based 10.9% (royalty +213.9% QoQ, over 1,600% YoY); MTP 10.6%; 1H PUF 11.6%, licensing +264.6%, royalty over 1,300% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: in Q2 2026 12-inch wafers contributed 62.5% of royalties (down 11.9% sequentially, up 12.3% YoY) and 8-inch wafers 37.5% (up 4.2% QoQ, up 1.2% YoY); 156 product tape-outs were completed in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: 12-inch 62.5% of royalties; 8-inch 37.5%; 156 product tape-outs in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: royalty revenue is expected to accelerate in Q3 and the second half of 2026 - several advanced-node products, including ADAS, AI accelerators, SSDs and networking, have begun entering mass production, and foundry wafer prices are gradually increasing. Chairman Charles Hsu: licensing will continue its strong momentum; royalty growth is expected to accelerate on higher ASP from new advanced-node applications, new application ramps, an expanding PUF royalty contribution and a growing mix of higher-royalty-rate MTP applications.

Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: Q2 royalty corresponds to foundry production in Q1, when mature-node foundry capacity utilization remained at a relatively low level and some customers went through seasonal inventory adjustment; from Q2 overall foundry capacity utilization began to improve.

Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: customers on 3 nanometer have already moved into mass production with several hundred wafers; royalty contribution is expected to become much more meaningful next year. Advanced-node projects already account for more than 50% of licensing NRE, as the licensing fee for a single advanced-node project is several times higher than the average project; royalty contribution is expected to increase meaningfully as these projects move into mass production.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 nm customers in mass production with several hundred wafers; advanced node more than 50% of licensing NRE

quarterly_data.signal: Chairman Charles Hsu: security IP has moved from stand-alone OTP / PUF / root of trust to fully integrated system-level security subsystems (encryption, software, firmware, anti-tampering); eMemory has licensed several major global memory manufacturers to integrate its security IP into AI data center SSDs as Caliptra-compliant security subsystems, and is working with several CXL chip makers to supply security IP and subsystems for AI server memory expansion. He expects potential licence fees and royalty to increase significantly.

Head of Digital Marketing Felix Hsu: first-half 2026 security IP licensing activity spanned CPUs, storage devices, optical communication ICs, FPGAs and high-speed interface chips, extending security IP from a single chip to multiple critical chips in AI servers. Chairman Charles Hsu: an increasing number of AI and data center chips are adopting the Caliptra security architecture, driven jointly by Microsoft, Google, Intel, AMD and NVIDIA.

Chairman Charles Hsu: 1T Flash (NeoFlash / Logic Flash) is in platform development and verification with several foundry partners, each progressing according to plan; customers may begin mass production next year. Standalone development focuses first on NOR Flash; after foundry partners bring standalone NOR Flash into mass production, eMemory may extend 1T Flash into a NAND Flash architecture.

Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: AI data center power architecture upgrades (400V / 800V HVDC) benefit eMemory as its OTP (analog trimming, power-control settings, product ID) and MTP IP are integrated into power management, power control and analog mixed-signal chips; customers have started to move into mass production and contribution is expected to expand in coming quarters.

Chairman Charles Hsu: eMemory continues to develop and qualify next-generation OTP and PUF-based hardware security for 2 nanometer Gate-all-around and sub-2 nanometer nodes. Director of Finance Joseph Hsia: its OTP technology has been adopted by U.S. customers for low Earth orbit satellite applications.
